function: End-to-end learning of an OFDM bit-stream link: BS-DNN modulation, TX-SIM and RX-SIM phase shifts (wave-domain precoding and combining), UE-DNN demodulation, trained for BER (p. 7-8).
system: 28 GHz, 100 MHz, 32 subcarriers; BS 4x4 antennas with 3-layer TX-SIM; 3 UEs, 3x3 antennas and 3-layer RX-SIM each; 100 units per layer; stacked metasurfaces (p. 3, 10).
method: Autoencoder-style E2E network (BS-DNN, trainable SIM phase layers, UE-DNN), BCE loss, AdamW; base model on statistical CSI, then transfer-learning fine-tuning on instantaneous CSI (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: geometric multipath channel, 100 scatterers, path loss and shadowing from [43], scatterers generated as in [42]; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurements (p. 4-5, 10-11).
test_conditions: Base model trained on statistical CSI, then transfer-learning fine-tuning on each random instantaneous channel; BER averaged over 100 Monte Carlo runs, swept over transmit power and system sizes (p. 10-12).
baselines: Massive MIMO OFDM (256T49R, 256T81R, 196T49R) whose design is not described; SIM vs DPSIM variants; fixed-power versus random-power training; transfer versus direct training (p. 11-12).
metrics: BER versus transmit power for each system size and training strategy; BCE training loss versus epochs (p. 10-12).
complexity: Number of parameters O(ML + NKJ + D^2HJ) and forward complexity O(Nc(M^2L + N^2KJ) + D^2HJ) for SIM; about twice for DPSIM (p. 9-10).
openness: none; the footnote on p. 1 reads Simulation code and picture: with no link (p. 1).
q1_support: p. 4: "the proposed SIM-assisted E2E OFDM system utilizes a geometric multi-path channel model" - an own simulator with S scatterers (Table II, p. 10); only the path loss follows [43] (p. 11); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "First, the EMNN uses statistical CSI to train a base model. Then, multiple sets of instantaneous channels are randomly generated" and fine-tuned by transfer learning; p. 11: "the transfer learning-based training method can achieve comparable performance to direct training, while significantly reducing the training time".
q3_support: p. 11: "an E2E OFDM system with 16T9R can achieve comparable performance to a massive MIMO OFDM system with 256T49R" - the benchmark's design (classical or learned) is never described, the other curves are variants of the proposed system, and no earlier learned E2E OFDM method of p. 2 is simulated.
q4_support: p. 9: "the number of parameters is on the order" of O(D^2 HJ) for the DNNs; p. 10: "the overall computational complexity of a single forward propagation" is O(Nc(M^2 L + N^2 KJ) + D^2 HJ).
q5_support: p. 1: "Simulation code and picture:" - the footnote ends with no link or DOI, no data link appears elsewhere, and the channel data are simulated (p. 4-5).
notes: Area 1 by the main-metric rule: the goal is to recover the transmitted bits (p. 7) and the only metric is BER; the same network also trains the TX and RX SIM phase shifts (area 3), so the reviewer may prefer area 3. ris is 1 because the stacked intelligent metasurface (SIM, and dual-polarized DPSIM) is a RIS of the stacked type. q2 is 1 because the base model trained on statistical CSI is fine-tuned by transfer learning on each new random instantaneous channel (p. 10-11); the fine-tuned model is tested on the same channel it was adapted to, and sweeps of system size are trained separately, so the reviewer should confirm. q3 is 0 because the massive MIMO OFDM benchmark is never described. q5 is 0 because the footnote Simulation code and picture: on p. 1 has no link in this PDF.
